findings.measurement: The three hashes listed under 'Taken against' still match exactly: plan 47df412d…, claim register 1a16f751…, and check-completeness 6c52a5f9…. Nevertheless the package result moved from 1/49 to 2/55 because those three hashes do not bind the package checker's actual freeze, blueprint, review, and artifact inputs.
findings.whyItIsAProblem: This is more than a stale historical number. The staging block claims its listed hashes let a signer test whether the captured values still hold, but all listed hashes match while the captured package result is false. That recreates the document's own named failure mode: recorded measurement presented with a guard that does not cover the measurement.
findings.proposedRepair: Correct every present-tense one-finding statement while retaining the old capture as explicitly superseded. For any future package capture, bind at least the exact freeze and blueprint hashes plus a deterministic manifest/digest of every referenced artifact and review that PC-7 grades, or retain only the command and require live output rather than publishing a partially pinned snapshot.
findings.applyWhenRationale: The live result contradicts the prose and the stated guard is demonstrably insufficient. No freeze anchor is touched.

findings.measurement: The live freeze table has eight rows: RunId, sealed-Run manifest identity, EvidenceDigest, finding fingerprint, FactViewId, cache/regeneration keys, executionPlanCommitment, and subjectScopeCommitment. Lines 1311-1315 then name two related gaps. The current finite named set is therefore ten, not nine. findings.whyItIsAProblem: The blueprint is the implementer's escalation map. Its finite count and enumeration omit a load-bearing commitment whose freeze row says two implementations can pass every existing vector while choosing opposite meanings. The general property at freeze lines 1324-1329 makes escalation technically permissible, but it does not repair the blueprint's explicit claim that all named items are present.
findings.proposedRepair: Add executionPlanCommitment to blueprint §5.1, change the current named total to ten, and update every current-tense 'nine' reference. Preserve historical nine-item measurements as dated history and distinguish them from the current set.
findings.applyWhenRationale: This is a measured enumeration error with direct implementation consequences. The affected text is outside all six freeze anchors.

quotedEvidence.quote: EvidenceDigest and RunId have full recipes at evidence.v10
v10 publishes a framing for EvidenceDigest and RunId ... a framing is not a byte recipe

EvidenceDigest = SHA-256(DomainEnvelopeV1(... exact SemanticEvidenceV1 bytes)); RunId = SHA-256(DomainEnvelopeV1(... exact RunIdentityPreimageV1 bytes))

findings.measurement: A duplicate-key-rejecting recursive walk found exact producing expressions at $.canonicalWireGrammar.commitments.EvidenceDigest and $.canonicalWireGrammar.commitments.RunId. The artifact also publishes exact preimage bytes, lengths, and expected digests/IDs. What remains open is application and closure of the inputs those outer recipes consume, not the existence of the outer recipes themselves.
findings.whyItIsAProblem: An implementer cannot tell whether to port an existing outer encoding, wait for a recipe, or treat the entire identity as undefined. The current corpus alternates between 'full recipe exists but is unapplied' and 'only framing exists.' Those lead to different work and different design-delta thresholds.
findings.proposedRepair: Use one precise statement everywhere: the outer EvidenceDigest and RunId byte recipes exist in the unapplied evidence v10 candidate and reproduce its vectors; they are not live authority because their dependency closure and application are unresolved. Separate 'recipe exists' from 'recipe is applied and all inputs are derivable.'
findings.applyWhenRationale: The opposite descriptions are simultaneously present and the artifact resolves the narrow factual question. No anchor is involved.

findings.measurement: The DELIVERY rule is at $.typescriptSemanticSubstrate.providerProtocol.wireSchema.definitions.SubjectScopeV1.fields.subjectScopeCommitment. It is concrete but scoped to SnapshotFileSubjectV1 in the TypeScript substrate. The prose never reconciles whether that scoped rule satisfies the generic C-2 Coverage field for the whole v1 provider set.
findings.whyItIsAProblem: One passage says the product rule exists on a binding head; the implementation map says any computation would be invented. The missing scope reconciliation is exactly the kind of week-one fork the package is intended to prevent.

Then make the freeze table, blueprint escalation list, and port order use that same scope-qualified conclusion. Do not infer the architectural answer in prose.
findings.applyWhenRationale: The present statements conflict. The immediate repair is an honest scope statement; it need not and must not invent a new recipe.

quotedEvidence.quote: Status: working plan (for review) ... Edit this file as the plan is refined
This plan is guidance ... Prefer editing this file
recorded by 40 files ... seven ... checkers exit 2 ... Editing that file is not expensive; it is closed

findings.measurement: The plan remained at required SHA-256 47df412d… before, during, and after the audit. The freeze records 40 pinning files and seven executing checkers; this audit did not mutate-probe the plan because that would violate the absolute no-edit constraint.
findings.whyItIsAProblem: The plan's own live instruction directs a maintainer to perform the exact edit the freeze says requires a successor cycle. This is a dangerous instruction even though the later freeze outranks it, because the plan is still labelled authoritative in handoff material and its opening tells the reader to edit before they reach the freeze warning.
findings.proposedRepair: Do not edit these bytes. Create a §10 delta/successor that records the plan as immutable historical process input and points to the freeze and blueprint as current front doors; update the 40 dependent pins through that successor cycle.
findings.applyWhenRationale: Any direct repair touches the hard-pinned plan and invalidates recorded environments. A full successor/delta cycle is mandatory.

findings.measurement: Freeze §3's 16 physical lines contain 3,058 words and 25,897 characters; the TM row alone is one 10,227-character line. Blueprint's 17-line contract-to-module table contains 997 words; its C-2 row is 1,971 characters. The tables mix current head, verdict, disposition, every repair round, verifier limitations, and candidate successor history inside single cells.
findings.whyItIsAProblem: These are the reviewer and signer current-state ledgers, but their table structure no longer provides a table's core affordance: comparing rows and reading the current value independently of history. A signer must parse thousands of words of adjudication narrative to determine which short status at the start or end of a cell governs.
findings.proposedRepair: After signature, create a successor freeze/blueprint with a mechanically derived compact ledger: one row per surface containing current head+digest, current review verdict, current freeze disposition, blocking IDs, and a single history pointer. Move the existing forensic narratives verbatim to per-surface appendices or retained artifacts; do not erase withdrawals. Keep the compact ledger generated or checked against the authorities it summarizes.
findings.applyWhenRationale: The real repair is structural extraction and consolidation across signature-bound primary documents. It should be a §10 delta after the current payload hash is recorded. None of the six anchor strings needs to change.

findings.measurement: §7.1 spans 455 lines and 4,979 words. It contains seven withdrawal tokens and nine correction tokens, an eight-row current table, two related gaps, a 33-position property-level measurement, multiple superseded counts, three candidate generations, and an explicit statement that the section can no longer corroborate a candidate it discusses.
findings.whyItIsAProblem: This is the package's implementation-stop list, yet determining current truth requires reconstructing a chronology and set algebra spread across nearly five thousand words. The section itself admits the corroboration boundary was crossed. A reader can honestly preserve every correction and still be unable to answer the operational question: which exact fields are blocked now, why, and what authority must close each one.
findings.proposedRepair: After signature, retain the full forensic text unchanged in a history appendix and replace the current-facing portion with a compact derived closure matrix: field/gap, owning binding surface, producing rule exists, rule applied, unresolved dependency, current action, and evidence pointer. Make historical measurements explicitly dated snapshots rather than members of the current set.
findings.applyWhenRationale: Consolidating a 4,979-word correction chain is a large structural rewrite. It belongs in a successor delta after the signed payload is fixed. §7.1 contains none of the six freeze anchors.

highestValueFindings.whyHighestValue: The authoritative surface ledger is no longer a comparable current-state table; its longest row is 10,227 characters.
The implementation-stop section is 4,979 words and explicitly admits it can no longer corroborate the candidate it narrates.
The signer's staging guard remains hash-matched while the result it purports to guard has changed from one finding to two.

readerPathAssessment.signer: PARTIAL, NOT STANDALONE. Sections 9 and 11 contain the right ceremony, explicit exceptions, and unset signature fields. A signer can eventually determine what to run, but must also parse the 3,058-word §3 table and the 4,979-word §7.1 chain. The staging package result is stale even though every hash listed beside it still matches, so the only safe path is to ignore the captured package figures and rerun. The signer does not need all 81,234 words, but the documents do not give a compact, mechanically bound route through the subset they do need.
readerPathAssessment.implementer: PARTIAL, WITH MATERIAL FORKS STILL EXPOSED. The blueprint contains a strong data flow, crate ownership map, process boundaries, port order, and explicit escalation discipline. Those assets make implementation possible after freeze. They do not yet make the blueprint a safe short path: the first flow appears after 6,515 words, the week-one start after 19,042, the named gap count omits executionPlanCommitment, and the EvidenceDigest/RunId and subjectScopeCommitment descriptions conflict. An implementer must currently consult the freeze and binding JSON to disambiguate the blueprint, contrary to its stated role.
readerPathAssessment.reviewer: NOT COHERENT AS A CURRENT-STATE INDEX. The corpus is unusually honest about withdrawals and preserves falsifiable history, which is valuable. The cost has crossed the line the task asked to measure: current dispositions share single table cells with entire lineages, narrative files carry stale review states, and §7.1 says it can no longer corroborate the candidate it describes. A reviewer can audit a chosen claim by following artifacts and hashes, but cannot first discover the current claim set without reading most of the correction history. A compact derived ledger is the missing entry point.

whatIDidNotCheck: I did not edit, normalize, reflow, or typo-fix any source document, contract, or checker. This artifact is the sole write.

I did not independently prove every semantic claim in the binding JSON or reproduce every checker mutation/selftest suite. The required normal-mode commands were run and their specific results asserted; green output is treated only as checker-scope evidence.
I did not audit product implementation source, because this task is the architecture corpus and no implementation claim follows from it.

I did not perform a writing-quality audit of v1-slice.md, GORTEX-BORROW-REGISTER.md, TREE-ENDSTATE.md, logs, steering notes, or the hundreds of adjudication/review artifacts. v1-slice.md and three binding JSON files were read only to verify specific findings.
I did not validate external HTTP links or the content of the pinned Gortex repository; local relative links only were resolved.

I did not decide whether DELIVERY's TypeScript-specific subjectScopeCommitment rule is intended to govern the generic C-2 field. DRA-004 records that unresolved scope contradiction rather than inventing the answer.
I did not claim that evidence v10's outer digest recipes provide a complete live authority chain. DRA-003 distinguishes recipe existence from application and dependency closure.
I did not classify checkers by filename. Checker claims reported here come from their executed output or inspected behavior/source, and non-zero exits were accepted only with their named findings.

I did not treat the absence of additional findings as full coverage. The audit concentrated on contradictions, current-state reconstruction, ordering, role paths, measurable redundancy, local links, and checkable factual claims; it is not an exhaustive copy-edit of all 81,234 words.
